newsitem.title: FRANCE: French minister warns against Iraq escalation.
newsitem.headline: French minister warns against Iraq escalation.

text.p: French Defence Minister Charles Millon warned his American and British counterparts on Monday against an escalation of the military situation in Iraq and said he had delivered the same message to Baghdad.

"It is essential to avoid an escalation," Millon told U.S. Defence Secretary William Perry and British Defence Secretary Michael Portillo during talks in London, the French Defence Ministry said in a statement.
"France has very firmly delivered the same message to Baghdad," the statement said.
Millon told the two men France backed its allies and was particularly concerned about the safety of its pilots enforcing the no-fly zones over Iraq along with British and U.S. aviators.
But it said that any threat against the allies' planes should be answered by "a proportional response", according to the statement.

Millon said he believed the Iraqis had got the French message to leave allied aircraft alone, having suspended all military action in recent days after initially launching missiles against some U.S. aircraft.
The missile firings had prompted President Bill Clinton to send troops and aircraft to the region in possible preparation for additional military strikes against targets in Iraq.
Perry was in London after visiting Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Bahrain and Turkey in the past few days to secure support for a possible U.S. military showdown with Iraqi President Saddam Hussein.

France had distanced itself from U.S. cruise missile strikes on Iraq earlier this month aimed at punishing Saddam for sending troops into Kurdish areas of northern Iraq to back a Kurdish guerrilla movement which has since gained control over the area.
A Foreign Ministry spokesman confirmed on Monday that France had allowed American Stealth bombers to fly over its territory late last week en route to the Gulf for possible use against Iraq.

Separately, French Foreign Minister Herve de Charette met Kuwaiti Deputy Prime Minister Sheikh Sabah al-Ahmad al-Jaber al-Sabah in Paris and Sabah said afterwards that France continued to support its territorial integrity.

"I am happy to have confirmed the French position towards Kuwait," Sabah told reporters. "There is no disagreement within the coalition on the basis issues. If Kuwait feels threatened in its integrity, it has a right to ask for and accept support."

"We have the same view of things. We are closely watching Kuwait and the region's security and stability, and we hope to do all we can to reduce the causes of tension and restore calm," de Charette said.
France's decision not to openly back U.S. missile strikes against southern Iraq had raised speculation that the allied coalition which drove Iraq out of Kuwait in 1991 was falling apart.
